excerpt from passages from antiquity to feudalism by perry anderson 2 greece i classical antiquity 2 greece the emergence of the hellenic citystates in the aegean zone predates the classical epoch proper and only its outlines can be glimpsed from the unwritten sources available after the collapse of mycenean civilization about 1200 bc greece experienced a prolonged dark age in which literacy disappeared and economic and political life regressed to a rudimentary household stage the primitive and rural world portrayed in the homeric epics it was in the succeeding epoch of archaic greece from 800 to 500 bc that the urban pattern of classical civilization first slowly crystallized at some time before the advent of historical records local kingships were overthrown by tribal aristocracies and cities were founded or developed under the domination of these nobilities aristocratic rule in archaic greece coincided with the reappearance of longdistance trade mainly with syria and the east the adumbration of coinage invented in lydia in the 7th century and the creation of an alphabetic script derived from phoenicia urbanization proceeded steadily spilling out overseas into the mediterranean and euxine until by the end of the colonization period in the mid 6th century there were some 1500 greek cities in the hellenic homelands and abroad virtually none of them more than 25 miles inland from the coastline these cities were essentially residential nodes of concentration for farmers and landowners in the typical small town of this epoch the cultivators lived within the walls of the city and went out to work in the fields every day returning at night although the territory of the cities always included an agrarian circumference with a wholly rural population settled in it the social organization of these towns still reflected much of the tribal past from which they had emerged their internal structure was articulated by hereditary units whose kin nomenclature represented an urban translation of traditional rural divisions thus the inhabitants of the cities were normally organized in descending order of size and inclusiveness into tribes phratries and clans clans being exclusive aristocratic groups and phratries perhaps originally their popular clienteles little is known of the formal political constitutions of the greek cities in the archaic age since unlike that of rome at a comparable stage of development they did not survive into the classical epoch itself but it is evident that they were based on the privileged rule of a hereditary nobility over the rest of the urban population typically exercised through the government of an exclusive aristocratic council over the city the rupture of this general order occurred in the last century of the archaic age with the advent of the tyrants c 650510 bc these autocrats broke the dominance of the ancestral aristocracies over the cities they represented newer landowners and more recent wealth accumulated during the economic growth of the preceding epoch and rested their power to a much greater extent on concessions to the unprivileged mass of citydwellers the tyrannies of the 6th century in effect constituted the critical transition towards the classical polis for it was during their general period of sway that the economic and military foundations of greek classical civilization were laid the tyrants were the product of a dual process within the hellenic cities of the later archaic period the arrival of coinage and the spread of a money economy were accompanied by a rapid increase in the aggregate population and trade of greece the wave of overseas colonization from the 8th to the 6th centuries was the most obvious expression of this development while the higher productivity of hellenic wine and olive cultivation more intensive than contemporary cereal agriculture perhaps gave greece a relative advantage in commercial exchanges within the mediterranean zone the economic opportunities afforded by this growth created a stratum of newly enriched agrarian proprietors drawn from outside the ranks of the traditional nobility and in some cases probably benefiting from auxiliary commercial enterprises the fresh wealth of this group was not matched by any equivalent power in the city at the same time the increase of population and the expansion and disruption of the archaic economy provoked acute social tensions among the poorest class on the land always most liable to become degraded or subjected to noble estateowners and now exposed to new strains and uncertainties the combined pressure of rural discontent from below and recent fortunes from above forced apart the narrow ring of aristocratic rule in the cities the characteristic outcome of the resultant political upheavals within the cities was the emergence of the transient tyrannies of the later 7th and 6th centuries the tyrants themselves were usually comparative upstarts of considerable wealth whose personal power symbolized the access of the social group from which they were recruited to honours and position within the city their victory however was generally possible only because of their utilization of the radical grievances of the poor and their most lasting achievement was the economic reforms in the interests of the popular classes which they had to grant or tolerate to secure their power the tyrants in conflict with the traditional nobility in effect objectively blocked the monopolization of agrarian property that was the ultimate tendency of its unrestricted rule and which was threatening to cause increasing social distress in archaic greece with the single exception of the landlocked plain of thessaly small peasant farms were preserved and consolidated throughout greece in this epoch the different forms in which this process occurred have largely to be reconstructed from their later effects given the lack of documented evidence from the preclassical period the first major revolt against aristocratic dominance that led to a successful tyranny supported by the lower classes occurred in corinth in the mid 7th century where the bacchiadae family was evicted from its traditional grip over the city one of the earliest trading centres to flourish in greece but it was the solonic reforms in athens that furnish the clearest and best recorded example of what was probably something like a general pattern of the time solon not himself a tyrant was vested with supreme power to mediate the bitter social struggles between the rich and the poor which erupted in attica at the turn of the 6th century his decisive measure was to abolish debt bondage on the land the typical mechanism whereby smallholders fell prey to large landowners and became their the best in show it was another hard winter not that that was surprising for our small town our side of the dales hadnt seen a winter without snow for as long as anyone could remember in our old market town we never used to let it get to us though we were all in it together and everyone had everyones back i should mention now that at that time when i was still a kid i didnt really appreciate the role of the dacre family and their importance to our town they were the first family practically local royalty keith helen his wife and their twin daughters rebecca and isabelle the dacres were certainly the wealthiest in town with keith owning the biggest source of employment in the area dacres machinery ltd supplying farming and agricultural equipment to most of the yorkshire dales and cumbria helen was also wellestablished owning a beauty salon in the centre helen would be in every day the salon was open chatting cheerfully to everyone who came in this also allowed her to get to know nearly everything about nearly everyone in the community to say we had never spoken she nevertheless knew everything about my life she was always a showcase for her own salon perfectly set hair flawless make up and elaborately decorated nails long before nail bars were found on every street before christmas shed always have reindeer and snowmen or some such fancy painted onto her talons the girls rebecca and isabelle were in my little sisters year at school ordinary annoying girls like i thought of every girl back then just with posher toys than most of us it was the dacre family that started off the competitions my mum told me apparently keiths dad started the tradition or his dads dad every winter we would host a myriad of competitions to keep spirits high and attempt to smother the blues some felt at that time of year there was best soup in town best chilli in town and the usual christmas pudding and christmas cake bakeoffs the local wool shop organised a knitwear catwalk bombarding people with colourful jumpers throws blankets and a seemingly bottomless supply of hats no vested interest there then every pun intended it all changed when i was about twelve the last year before it all stopped the main competition that almost everyone took part in was the best snowman competition you will have seen scarecrow trails and scarecrow competitions in villages well we reckoned on getting creative with the predictable snow using the cold to warm the hearts of the community every household would chip in a couple of quid and then make snowmen in different shapes and sizes on a given day four appointed judges would walk around the town and score them the winning household would win half of the money paid in with the other half being donated to the winning households charity of choice this particular year however the dacre family would be absent they had decided that they would book a prechristmas trip to lapland so the girls could meet father christmas they wouldnt shut up about it and back then i just thought that they were annoying spoilt little brats keith informed the competitions committee that this year as they werent going to be there for the snowman competition that he would match the charity donation and give that to the charity the winning household picked the evening before they set off for lapland the dacres had a meal together in the local pub they were all excited for the adventures that were to come and keith was in such a good mood he left a threehundredpound float behind the bar for everyone to have a christmas drink on the dacre family much to the joy of everyone there especially my father they left in good spirits to trudge through the snow to the big house that looked down on the town from way up the hill a few days later and most of the town as they did every year had built their various snowmen all were in their front gardens or on the community greens for those that didnt have gardens like me my sister and i had sweated over ours for ages this was the first time id managed to get a third layer onto it to us then it was a work of art in retrospect it was terrible most snowmen had a sign often with a random pun relating to the theme of their build i put a grass skirt and a blonde wig on ours and called it hips dont lie after the song released by my preteen crush on shakira i thought my design was ruined by the fact my mum wouldnt let me put a bikini top on it so the streets were buzzing with people walking around excitedly looking at the builds and talking about which ones were their favourites the competitions committee judges including my mum were out in their stride making sure to view each one and mark their check lists and then they would leave a little board on a stick next to each build with a score out of ten the committee consisted of four as i said but this year they were accompanied by my sister and i as mum wouldnt leave us in the house alone after the last time the judges were always quick to get out and view the snowmen as soon as possible on the elected day so the weather didnt ruin the details they made their way to the second green and i struggled to keep my mouth shut as two of the judges awarded our masterpiece a pitiful three points then we were dragged up the hill to survey what wonders the dacres has created they had a montage a family of four large and elaborate snowmen in the front garden of their huge house all of which were wearing ornately patterned fluffy hats and scarves knitted at the wool shop the colours contrasted to the cold features of their faces consisting of rocks and pebbles for eyes and mouths and as everyone else they had put a sign at the bottom of the display this one reading best in show twelveyearold me was livid it didnt even look like they had used their own snow the figures were surrounded by immaculate pristine snow unmarred by footprint or dog wee like we had to contend with on the green but even as i opened my mouth to complain my mothers stern look silenced me it wasnt worth risking her wrath just before christmas presents were at stake june however another of the judges and owner of the wool shop cooed over them so festive such beautiful craftsmanship in the traditional snowflake patterns as she wrote 1010 on her score card this was the first time i had come to understand the concept of match rigging i dont like those whispered meredith my little sister clutching at the front of my jacket as she looked at the two snowmen representing the twins theyre spooky i thought she was daft feeling uneasy after all they were just snowmen nevertheless i gave her a brief hug she was only six after all and mum was watching the judges conferred worked out the average score and marked the board the dacres snowmen had an average score of 910 certain to win i had calculated that the kitty to the winners this year would be about a hundred and twenty after the charity donations nothing to the dacres but to someone like me like i said i was livid we all began to trudge back down the hill towards the town the cold stare of the four snowmen seemingly still unnerving meredith as she and i looked back one last time at them the bloody dacres even their bloody snowmen looked down on the rest of us that evening i shared my annoyance with my friends whilst playing halo 2 on x box live i told them about the fixed voting perhaps slightly exaggerating how mean the judges had been about their efforts as well as mine making out that only my mum was anything like fair then we came up with what we thought was a great idea each of us claimed to be going round to anothers house for a game instead meeting at the dark side of the green the stars were glimmering in clear patches of sky whilst the moon was surrounded by a nimbus of high thin cloud as our band of five positively scampered excitedly up the hill as we passed through the gates onto the drive amazed that they werent locked a sense of our own intended wrongdoing made me pause but only momentarily with childish glee we committed the funniest most shocking deed that our juvenile brains had dreamed up we spraypainted willies and boobs on to the snowmen did i imagine the snowmen staring down at us balefully i think i did did we then get distracted by what felt like acres of deep crisp pristine snow what kid could resist before we knew it we were playing our own version of halo in the garden using trees and benches as defence posts shrieking and giggling our voices echoed in the crisp night air carried away i reckoned i could go up against all of them like the masterchief as a flurry of snowballs pounded relentlessly into my face i realised just how wrong i was barely able to see and get my bearings i stumbled over towards the snowmen to take shelter behind their bulk reaching out from behind the montage to launch further missiles i suddenly felt my foot slip from under me and i slid down the side of the nearest snowman my mates of course laughed hysterically as a chunk of the snow from the arm fell with a heavy splat on top of my head winded by the fall i didnt realise how suddenly that laughter stopped as i tried to move i felt a sharp scratch close to my eye and then a sensation of the snow being raked from the top of my head as i finally sat up still feeling an odd pressure on the top of my head and more snow gave way i became aware of the horror on my friends faces all were seemingly staring at my head or above my head i tipped my face slowly back there were the unmistakable elaboratelymanicured fingernails of mrs dacre raking through my hair in absolute terror i kicked out blindly at the ground the snow the figure and with what seemed like a groan the rest of the snowman and its macabre contents fell back away from the next snowman along disturbed further snow fell away from the second figure and the tall dead form of mr dacre was revealed his face still contorted in horror i remember the sound of my own hysterical screaming ringing through the night before we charged still shrieking like possessed beings down the hill rousing the sleepy town chased by the wave of lights suddenly turned on in each house as our terror disturbed their peace all i remember of that christmas now is the sleepless nights when i would feel again and again the manicured nails of mrs dacre comb through my hair that and the endless questioning by police my parents silent compassion regarding the matter was one of the worst things their lack of anger just emphasised the true horror we had encountered the towns spirit died that day no competition could ever be brought back without evoking the ghost of four murder victims because although noone was charged it had to be murder they couldnt bury themselves in elaborately adorned carapaces of snow it was the lack of answers that scared the town the most forensics revealed no cause of death or deaths no drugs in their systems no stab wounds no petechial haemorrhaging their home surveillance footage claimed to be unaltered untampered with yet the snowmen seemingly appeared between one sweep of the grounds and the next suggesting everything was done within less than three minutes which is impossible no footprints other than ours were found there was no sign of anyone other than the dacres entering their grounds that night nothing was ever the same after that as i said i had never appreciated what the dacres did for the town people lost heart their little paradise was ruined employment opportunities dwindled and many my father included lost their jobs and were obliged to move away to find work thats what we ended up doing too a couple of my mates from that night stayed the five of us were never all together again the big house never found a buyer if you had enough money to afford that you wouldnt be moving to a dying town why bring this up now i had an email from an old mate whos still in the town one who was with me that night all it had was a picture of what was once the dacres garden there was a montage a family of four large and elaborate snowmen in the front garden of the huge abandoned house all wearing ornately patterned fluffy hats and scarves and the figures were surrounded by immaculate pristine snow unmarred by footprint a sign at the bottom of the display read still the best in
